its_31_reported_tables_read_again_with_t.note: two readings gave another choice on the repeat: the memory of confirmed laws is given five seconds, and the machine was shared

how: python scripts/run_small_tables.py dev --out DIR --laws 120 --workers 2 ; collect. Laws of the invented-law grammar at one and two inputs (seed 2026112401), noise 0, 1 % and 5 % of the target's size, no search stage in either arm. Each law given is scored on 400 clean rows: accurate at R2 0.999, and whether it has the true law's form.
reading: Without a search stage, the route in force called directly gave the true form on 2 of 120 small tables and reported nothing; by its own rule it reports only behind a search stage. So this arm is the first pass alone.
First run: the reading reported 31 laws and 3 were wrong (10 %), above the 5 % a referee is allowed. All three had four rows for each fitted constant, on tables of 8 and 12 rows.

Second run, with the rule of five rows a constant: 17 reported, 0 wrong, 10 with the true form. The true form on 17 tables and an accurate law on 48. It gained the true form on 15 tables against the first pass and lost it on 0.
The rule was chosen on these tables, so no wrong report among 17 is not a test of it. PREREG-REAL-TABLES-2026-11 tests it on tables drawn afterwards.
7 of the 17 true forms were chosen from the memory of confirmed laws, which the first pass alone does not have. The memory was built on laws of this grammar.
At 5 % noise the reading reported nothing on 36 tables and was accurate on 2. At 8 rows it reported nothing with the rule. Small tables at that noise or size are beyond it.
Four tables came out differently in the second run than in the first, beyond what the rule changes: the memory's five seconds make a reading depend on machine load.
About 48 seconds a table on two cores.
